pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin rinds are soft satin with faint long streaks, and the leaves are quiet; gloss and micro-texture fall within the real range. B: the topiary is covered in hundreds of hard, crisp, equally shiny little leaves, with the same lacquered highlight repeated on every leaf. Detail, micro-texture and gloss share (0.437) are all above the real range.
pairs.fix: Draw the topiary as soft rounded masses of foliage. Merge most leaves into a smooth matte surface, show only a few larger leaf shapes near the top of each tier, and put one broad soft highlight on each tier, not a shine on every leaf.

pairs.difference: A: the cooler is matte red plastic, the can lids are thin metal with a crisp rim, and the ice is translucent, so it has a real gloss mix. B: the lion is waxy smooth marble with thin grey veins on the plinth and soft blurred mane strands. Its numbers sit at the low edge of the real range, but soft smooth surfaces are also what real cards show. My vector gives no firm reason to choose.

A: the bat's whole body and wing edges carry a dense, even felt-like fur noise with no sheen at all. Gloss share of 0.006 is below the real range, and the texture reads like a photographed plush, unlike the clean surfaces on real cards. B: the envelope paper is soft and smooth with a quiet emboss on the stamp and postmark. The tiny village is crisp and busy, which pushes detail slightly high, but the materials stay within the card language.
pairs.fix: Paint the bat's body as a smooth soft shape with no individual fur hairs, only a slight fuzzy edge. Add one broad soft sheen on top of the head and body, and give the wings a light satin shine.

pairs.difference: A: the shoes have a fine, even dot mesh on the toe, smooth rubber soles and glossy plastic-like laces, a clear mix of finishes at small scale. B: the cauldron body carries a fine diagonal scratchy noise through the shoulder highlight and the dark teal sheen, like a grainy filter over the metal rather than a clean smooth gradient.
pairs.fix: Make the cauldron smooth dark cast iron with clean soft gradients and one soft-edged highlight on the shoulder. Remove all fine scratches, grain and speckle from the metal.

pairs.difference: A: the lamp has dark painted metal with soft highlights and translucent frosted glass with a clear inner bulb. B: the candelabra has smooth gold with long soft reflections and matte cream wax. Both separate matte from shiny well, neither shows noise or smear, and the numbers are close and in range.

A: the door frame has big decorative dark grain lines, the door's blue is mottled, the plaster has drawn cracks, and every ivy leaf has a crisp glossy highlight. All three surface measures are far above the real range (gloss 0.51, micro 0.0447). B: the stone and roof tiles are brush-textured and also glossy-high, but much closer to real and with larger, calmer marks.
pairs.fix: Make the door frame smooth painted wood with only a few faint fine grain lines. Keep the blue door panels clean and even, leave the plaster plain with no cracks, and simplify the ivy into fewer soft matte leaves with a highlight only on a few.

pairs.difference: A: the headstone has a fine even grain over all the stone, drawn hairline cracks and fuzzy moss with fine speckle, the kind of small surface detail added on generated cards. B: the slide is plain smooth plastic with soft gradients and tiny wood lines only under the deck, as quiet as the real cards, though very simple.
pairs.fix: Paint the headstone as smooth, softly shaded stone with no speckle or grain. Keep one simple chipped edge instead of thin cracks, and make the moss a smooth soft rounded green shape rather than fuzzy hairs.

pairs.difference: A: the silver stand has clean polished highlights against a soft smooth glass orb, with crisp edges and a clear glossy-versus-soft split. B: the cans and bottles behind the glass have melted smeary labels, the glass is spattered with tiny droplets, and the blue cabinet is uniform plastic. The droplets and smear are the giveaway at 2×.
pairs.fix: Draw the cans and bottles with clean simple labels and sharp edges. Remove the small droplets from the glass and use one soft diagonal reflection instead. Keep the cabinet satin, with brighter polished metal only on the handle and tray.

pairs.difference: A: the mower has smooth red satin plastic, matte rubber tires and thin dull metal tubes, a good range with clean quiet surfaces. B: the broom straw is big chunky glossy blades with a hard shine on each, the handle is uniformly lacquered, and the floor has strong grain and dark plank lines. Detail, micro-texture and gloss (0.275) are all above the real range.
pairs.fix: Draw the bristles as many thin fine straws with a matte dry finish, grouped into soft clumps. Make the handle satin wood with one quiet highlight, and keep the floorboards smooth with faint grain.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin is covered in very fine, dense, even parallel grain streaks on the lid and side, like the generated desks in the lessons, with only the brass handle shining. B: the chair has sparser, softer grain on the back and arms like the real wooden desk, but the wood and cushion share a similar lacquered shine. The gap is small; both are streaky.
pairs.fix: Paint the coffin wood as smooth soft reddish-brown with only a few faint, long, broad grain lines. Remove the dense thin streaks, and add a soft sheen along the top edge of the lid.

pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin has smooth waxy rind with a few tiny pores and a soft sheen, quiet like real cards, though gloss is at the low end. B: the jacket is soft foam-like cloth with no stitches or weave and crisp shiny badges, with detail just above range because of the badges. Both finishes fit the smoothed real look, so my vector gives no reason to choose.

A: the towel is covered in dense photographic terry-loop texture across every stripe, with folds shaded like a real photo. Detail (0.0995) and micro-texture (0.0277) are far above the real range. B: the coral is smooth and soft with shallow, modest dimples, and the dark rocks are matte. That matches the real coral card's quiet finish, though the rocks are a little painterly.
pairs.fix: Paint the towel as a smooth soft fabric shape with clean stripes. Replace the terry loops with a light, sparse hint of soft fluffiness and a few soft fold shadows, with no fine pile over the whole surface.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away by adding surface detail at too fine a scale: all-over grain, felt fuzz, photographic terry, scratchy noise on metal, dense thin wood-grain streaks, tiny droplets and a separate highlight on every leaf or straw. Real cards keep surfaces smooth and quiet, with broad soft gradients, one or two large highlights, sparse restrained marks and a clear split between matte and shiny parts. Pairs with no such excess were too close to call.
